eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and German Weather Service indicate a warm southerly flow under relatively stable conditions for Munich on August 16, supporting afternoon maxima near 31–33 °C, yet with notable spread arising from potential afternoon convective showers or increased cloud cover that could cap temperatures at 30 °C or allow brief clearing to 32 °C. Recent ensemble runs show modest disagreement on instability timing and coverage, consistent with the market’s tight clustering among the 30–32 °C outcomes and lower probabilities assigned to 34 °C or higher. Historical August climatology in southern Bavaria places typical daily highs in the mid-20s °C, so current guidance reflects a modest positive anomaly driven by the ongoing warm advection pattern. Updated model runs and satellite trends over the next 24 hours will likely narrow the range ahead of resolution.

Official PAGASA guidance and ensemble forecasts indicate daytime maxima in the 29–32°C range under these conditions, consistent with historical August averages near 31°C but suppressed by reduced insolation and evaporative cooling from precipitation. Recent model runs show minimal day-to-day shifts, supporting trader emphasis on 30°C (46.5%) over 31°C (27.5%) or 29°C (18%), with only low odds assigned to extremes given the stable monsoon pattern and lack of clearer skies or stronger heating expected before resolution.
